correctness.rationale: For N>=4, removing two distinct cycle edges yields path components of j and N-j patches. Independent Bernoulli ignition with q=1-p saves j q^j+(N-j)q^(N-j) in expectation, so B_j=N-H_j. The exact adjacent difference factorizes as q^j(1-q)[sum_{a=1}^{N-2j-2} q^a+(N-j)q^(N-2j-1)-j]; its bracket is strictly increasing from -j to positive endpoint for j<floor(N/2), hence a unique crossing r_j in (0,1). The nonstandard global argument extends j to x and writes h(x)=exp(-Nt/2)[N cosh(ty)-2y sinh(ty)], y=N/2-x,t=-log q. Derivative sign is Nt/2-1-z coth z, a strictly decreasing function of z, so the sampled H_j has no strict valley nor three consecutive equal values. A reversal or equality of adjacent thresholds would create precisely such a valley or triple tie, forcing all r_j strictly increasing and each unique globally optimal gap on (r_{j-1},r_j). Boundary N=4 and odd/even N are included. Independent exact rational checks and numerical root isolation found N=8 thresholds 0.469138898665, 0.569240819317 and 0.6; exact point checks confirm all four gaps. Finite N sample checks supplement rather than establish the all-N argument.
residual_risks: Assumes a fully symmetric ring, perfect breaks and one-season independent ignition; no claims about operational wildfire behavior under wind or correlated fuel.

value.rationale: Exact optimal placement across all ignition risks in a mathematically natural minimal network partition provides a complete phase diagram and excludes skipped geometries and triple ties. Although the homogeneous ring is a stylized model, the strict staircase is not merely obvious equal spacing: at high ignition probability adjacent cuts win, all intermediate gaps become uniquely best, and equal spacing is optimal only below a sharp threshold. This structural calculation is potentially reusable as a reliability/fragmentation benchmark.
residual_risks: The conclusion is a mathematical expectation result for a toy homogeneous landscape, not an empirically calibrated wildfire recommendation.
